Commentary.Commentary: Right then! David Miller goes on to the podium and lifts the series trophy along with his teammates, who rejoice and pose for a team photo. With this, the white-ball tour comes to an end after a 1-1 draw in the ODIs, South Africa have gone from 1-0 down to clinch the T20I series 2-1. There is still a lot of action left in this tour but before the focus shifts to the Test series, The Hundred will begin on the 3rd of August. The first Test match will be played after a prolonged break at Lord's on the 17th of August and will begin at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT). Our build-up for that game will begin much sooner. Do join us then. Take care and goodbye!

The winning captain of South Africa, David Miller says it's a privilege to play 100 caps for his country. Adds that he thought Rilee Rossouw and Reeza Hendricks batted brilliantly and got them off to a great start. Mentions they quickly forgot about the first game and is happy they bounced back in this series. Adds that Tristan Stubbs is really gifted and mentions that he has showcased it in domestic cricket but it is incredible to see him do it on the big stage. Mentions that everyone in the team is making a remarkable effort. Whenever they are in trouble, someone or the other put their hand up and that's what they need at the moment.

English skipper, Jos Buttler says that they thought it was a big score to chase down but he was confident and they always look to challenge themselves with the bat. Adds that they played disappointingly and lacked intent and the opposition bowled well too. Mentions that this summer has been a realization and they haven't performed up to their potential and have to work on their shortcomings. Says that they have a bit of time to go away and reflect before heading on to the big tournament and they need to have confidence in their players. Mentions that the three T20Is in Australia before the World Cup will be crucial for the team.

Reeza Hendricks WINS THE PLAYER OF THE SERIES AWARD for his incredible effort with the bat throughout the series. He says that he is very happy with his performance. Mentions that overall it is all about team performance and he got great support from his team-mates. Adds whenever he comes out at the crease, he aims at putting up a solid performance and leaving a stamp of authority. Ends by saying they have definiately improved since the defeat in the first game.

Tabraiz Shamsi (4-0-24-5) is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his match-winning spell. Shamsi says that he really enjoyed himself today but all credit goes to the batters and the bowlers who laid the foundation for him. Adds that it is all about helping each other and sometimes his good work helps others and vice-versa. Says that he keeps in his mind about bouncing back and looks to better his outings from the previous games. Adds that his wife told him to get four wickets in the game and hence his celebrations were a bit more animated when he got those wickets.

Moeen Ali wins the Player of the Summer, an award that he gets for producing the most consistent performances throughout the English summer. He starts by saying he has played decently but his side is not on the bright side. Mentions his role in the side is to float around, and go hard whenever he comes out on the track but it did not pay off.
Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Jos Buttler won the toss and opted to bowl first and given the dimensions of the ground, the par score seemed to be around 170 or so. England made a fast start but Reeza Hendricks and Rilee Rossouw counter-attacked brilliantly before the likes of Aiden Markram and David Miller took on the bowlers. Even with a couple of stop-starts due to rain, the South African batters managed to find the fence with regularity. Only David Willey was on top of his game with the ball for England and Chris Jordan had a rare forgettable outing as he conceded more than 50 runs. With a big score to chase, England needed to click in the Powerplay but the visitors never let them get any sort of momentum in the chase. Their batters were blown away by the opposition bowlers and it was Tabraiz Shamsi who picked up five wickets to seal an easy victory for the Proteas.

England have had a miserable white-ball summer and apart from the mauling of the Netherlands, they have come up short against the heavyweights of World Cricket. Jos Buttler, who was having a stellar year up until taking on full-time captaincy of the white-ball team must now feel dejected, having failed to win a single series at home. Both openers looked vulnerable and got out cheaply and once the middle order was exposed, the required rate had climbed up too high. Caught in between staying at the crease and keeping up with the scoring rate pressure, the English batters were sent back to the hut one by one and barely managed to cross 100 runs. Only Jonny Bairstow managed to bat for a longer period of time but all in all, it has been a very disappointing batting display from the hosts, who were even mocked by their own fans.

Given the way South Africa started this T20I series, conceding plenty of runs and being poor in the field, this has been some performance from them. They bowled well and hanged on to all their catches and there were plenty of them in this game. Keshav Maharaj gave them a good start with the ball but after that, every bowler that came into the attack, played his part and picked up wickets. Both spinners were outstanding but Tabraiz Shamsi was on a different level altogether as he picked up a five-wicket haul in a T20I game and that indeed is a rare sight. The pacers were economical and the Proteas will be proud of the way they have bounced back here after losing the first game of the series by a big margin.

This has been as dominant as it gets from South Africa as they have ripped apart the English batting order to seal a memorable comeback series win, their first T20I series victory in England. The match started with a wicket-maiden from David Willey but since then it has been all Proteas.

OUT! CAUGHT! Keshav Maharaj takes the final wicket of the innings. It is floated and full, on off. Jonny Bairstow goes for the slog-sweep but gets it off the top-edge. It goes high towards deep mid-wicket. David Miller settles under it and takes a sharp catch. SOUTH AFRICA WIN THE GAME BY 90 RUNS.
Commentary.Howout: c David Miller b Keshav Maharaj

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Something for the English fans to cheer. It is full and on off. Jonny Bairstow gets low and sweeps it to deep square leg for a boundary.
Quicker and full, on off. Jonny Bairstow tries to sweep it away but gets an inside edge on his pads.
Fuller, on off. Jonny Bairstow sweeps it to deep square leg and denies for the single.
Reece Topley is the last man in for England.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tabraiz Shamsi picks up his fifth wicket. He is absolutely delighted and is robbed by his team-mates. He has come back like a champion. England lose their ninth. It is short, on off. Adil Rashid pulls it to long on. Aiden Markram takes an easy catch running in at long on.
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Tabraiz Shamsi

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller, outside off. Adil Rashid moves to that side and blocks it out.
Adil Rashid is the next man in.

OUT! LBW! It looks plumb. Tabraiz Shamsi appeals and raises his dreaded finger in a flash. Chris Jordan thinks it is missing the wickets and goes for the review. It is tossed up, around off, turning in off the deck a touch. Chris Jordan is caught inside his crease and gets rapped on his pads. The on-field decision is OUT. The UltraEdge confirms no bat and the Ball Tracking shows that it is umpire's call on ball hitting the wicket. Tabraiz Shamsi gets his fourth.
Fuller, on off. Chris Jordan lofts it towards long off for a brace.

FOUR! Full and wide outside off. Chris Jordan stays back and throws his bat at it. It goes off the splice towards backward point. Lungi Ngidi tries to chase it but it evades his effort and races away to the boundary.
Floated and full, on the stumps. Jordan plays it back to the bowler.
Swing and a miss! This is short and around off, Jonny Bairstow has a swing across the line but the ball goes under his bat.
Just short of a length and over middle, this is pulled away without much timing through mid-wicket for a run.
Fuller in length and around off, this is driven to the left of the man at the extra cover fence and they come back for two with ease.
FOUR! Slashed away! Good length and a bit wide, Chris Jordan throws his hands at it. One hand comes off the bat as the ball is sliced over backward point for a boundary.
This is full and straight, Jonny Bairstow uses his wrists to turn it through mid-wicket for a single.

NOT OUT! Chris Jordan stays at the crease. It is full, sliding into the pads. Chris Jordan stays back and tries to work it to the leg side but misses. He gets pinged on his pads. No interest shown from the umpire. Miller takes the review but it does not work in their favour. They collect a leg bye.

Review! David Miller takes his time to decide and eventually takes a review for lbw. There is no such excitement from the bowler. The original decision is not out. It is pitching outside off, impact is umpire's call. Chris Jordan is safe.
It is full, on the pads, Jonny Bairstow nudges it to mid-wicket. The batters push hard for the first one and get two.
It is floated and full, on off. Jordan hits it to mid off for a single.
Chris Jordan is the new man at the crease. A slip, leg slip and short mid-wicket in position for the Hat-Trick ball.

OUT! TIMBER! Two in tow for Tabraiz Shamsi and is running away in celebration. This is beautifully bowled by Shamsi, on a nagging length and drifted onto middle. This is the variation as it goes straight on. David Willey gets down low to slog it away but misses and the ball castles into middle stump. Willey departs for agolden duck and Shamsi is on a hat-trick.
David Willey comes in at number 8.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tabraiz Shamsi has the last laugh here! This is dragged down a bit and around off. Sam Curran rocks back and looks to pull it down the ground and gets a decent connection on it. The ball flies down the throat of the man at long off and Aiden Markram over there takes a comfortable catch. Shamsi has two and South Africa are running away with the game.
Commentary.Howout: c Aiden Markram b Tabraiz Shamsi

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up, outside off and this is pushed towards cover.
SIX! This is dragged down from Shamsi, on middle and leg, Sam Curran rocks back and muscles it over the mid-wicket fence for the first maximum of the innings.

FOUR! Finally, Rilee Rossouw is caught napping and England do get a boundary. This is the knuckle-ball, on the shorter side and over leg stump. Jonny Bairstow plays a controlled pull shot behind square but Rossouw doesn't pick it up and the ball ends up in the fence.
On a nagging length, angling it into middle. Sam Curran looks to play it off the back foot but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls onto the off side and a single is stolen.
Pitches it up on middle, Jonny Bairstow heaves it away towards deep backward square leg for only another single. England need a bit of inspiration here and they certainly need a lot of boundaries.
On a hard length and around off, this is chopped towards cover-point for a quick single.
Length, around the top of off, Curran goes back and pushes it towards the bowler.
This is on a fullish length, from around the wicket and close to the off pole. Sam Curran looks to punch it out on the off side but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Full and on off, pushed down the ground for a single.
Sam Curran is the new man in. England need 127 runs off 49.

OUT! CAUGHT! England are folding like a pack of cards here. Tabraiz Shamsi with his slowest delivery of the game, floats it up, full and around off. Liam Livingstone's eyes lit up as he looks to break the shackles and decides to take it on. Livingstone can't quite get under it and hits it flat towards long off. Keshav Maharaj over there takes a good low catch and England have lost half their side. 126 needed now off 48 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Keshav Maharaj b Tabraiz Shamsi

Commentary.Commentary: Brilliant stop from Tabraiz Shamsi. Flatter and on leg stump, Liam Livingstone looks to power it back past the bowler but fails to do so.
Tossed up, on middle and leg, Bairstow plays the reverse sweep through covers and collects a single.

A bit of a mix-up in the middle and out come the 'Boos' from the crowd. On the shorter side, around middle, this is played off the back foot and through mid-wicket for one. They think about two but recognize that it is Stubbs fielding out there and hence, settle for one.
This is flatter and on the pads, Livingstone flicks it straight towards short fine leg.
Fuller and around middle, driven through long on for a single.
Back of a length, around middle and leg, Bairstow hops back and plays it behind square on the leg side for just another single.
It's that man Stubbs again! Around the top of off, Bairstow drives on the up but can't get it past Stubbs at short extra cover who makes a brilliant stop down to his right.
Length, around off and this is driven through cover for a single.
What happened here? This is on a good length, outside off. Liam Livingstone looks to get forward but the ball just takes off and Livingstone is taken completely aback.
This is potched up and on off, Bairstow pushes it down to long off for a single.
Liam Livingstone is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! OH MY GOD! WHAT A TAKE FROM STUBBS! Aiden Markram takes a wicket here but all the credit goes to Tristan Stubbs. It is tossed up, around off. Moeen Ali tries to flick it to leg side but closes the face a bit early. The ball lobs to the left of covers off the leading edge. Tristan Stubbs is way away from the ball, it looks like the ball will land safely. Stubbs sprints to his left, dives to that side with his left-hand stretched out and takes a blinder. South Africa are on the driving seat now.
Commentary.Howout: c Tristan Stubbs b Aiden Markram

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter, on off. Jonny Bairstow pulls it hard towards mid on. One taken.
Flatter, outside off. Ali punches it through covers for one more.
Jonny Bairstow comes down to this full delivery and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single. The run rate continues to creep up.
Floated and full, on the stumps. Moeen Ali drives it down to long off and rotates the strike.
Darted on the pads, Jonny Bairstow flicks it to mid-wicket for a single.
The part-timer, Aiden Markram to roll his arm now.
A successful over by Andile Phehlukwayo. A wicket and just four runs off it. It is full and on off. Jonny Bairstow drives it to mid off and crosses.
A length ball, around off, Moeen Ali stays back and punches it through covers for one.
Fuller, on off. Ali blocks it back to the bowler.
Moeen Ali walks in with England completely on the back foot.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another man bites the dust. Dawid Malan tries to break the shackles but holes out instead. It is quicker and full, on the pads, Dawid Malan thinks of using the pace to his benefit here but it does not pay off. He flicks it aerially towards deep square leg and does not get enough distance on it. Anrich Nortje charges towards the ball from the deep and takes an incredible catch diving forward.
Commentary.Howout: c Anrich Nortje b Andile Phehlukwayo

Commentary.Commentary: Full length, angled into the pads, Jonny Bairstow flicks it to the leg side for an easy single.
Andile Phehlukwayo follows the batter to the leg side with a short one. Dawid Malan pulls it to deep mid-wicket. They take one.
Andile Phehlukwayo to have a bowl now.
Floated and full, on off. Malan gets low and drags his sweep to deep square leg for another single. A tidy start for Tabraiz Shamsi.
Floated and full, on the pads, Jonny Bairstow flicks it to mid-wicket for just a single. He wanted the second run but was sent back by Malan.
Outside off. Malan punches it to covers. The fielder misfields and the batters take one.
Tossed up, full and around off. Dawid Malan tries to go for the reverse-sweep but misses it to wear it on the pads.
This is quicker, on the pads. Jonny Bairstow whips it to deep square leg for a single.
Floated and full, outside off. Jonny Bairstow stays back and slaps it through covers for two runs.
Tabraiz Shamsi to bowl for the first time in this game.
Slightly short, on off. Malan pulls it to deep square leg. The batters push hard and get two runs. 5 runs off the over.
Fuller, on off. Bairstow drives it through covers for another single.
This one is on the pads, Malan flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
This is full and on off, Jonny Bairstow strokes it away through wide mid off for a single.
Quicker and flatter, close to the off pole, Jonny Bairstow taps it towards cover-point.
Flatter delivery, around off, this is kept out on the off side.
Keshav Maharaj (2-0-12-1) is back on.
Good length, around off. Malan blocks it out watchfully. A successful wicket from Nortje comes to an end.
Anrich Nortje fires in a yorker, on middle and leg. Jonny Bairstow digs it out towards square leg and crosses for a single.
NO BALL! Too high says the umpire. It is short ball, on middle. Jonny Bairstow ducks under it. The umpire signals a no ball for height. A Free Hit to follow.
Fuller, on off. Jonny Bairstow eases it back to the bowler. Anrich Nortje gets low and collects it in a flash.
A length ball, around off, nips in off the deck with some extra bounce. Jonny Bairstow stays back and tries to defend it out but misses. The ball goes over the stumps and into the keeper's mitts.

FOUR BYES! Anrich Nortje welcomes Bairstow with a sharp bouncer. Jonny Bairstow ducks under it. It is also very high for Quinton de Kock and it goes away to the fine leg fence. The umpire signals a bye.
Jonny Bairstow walks in at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Jason Roy's poor form continues in this series. Anrich Nortje comes back into the attack and strikes instantly. South Africa are well ahead in this game now. Anrich Nortje fires in a length ball, on middle and leg, Jason Roy makes room and tries to slap it away. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards Quinton de Kock behind the sticks who pouches the ball comfortably. Jason Roy trudges back to the dug out.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Anrich Nortje

Commentary.Commentary: Change. Anrich Nortje (1-0-10-0) is back into the attack now.
Ends the over with another slower ball. This is on a length and outside off, Roy just stabs it towards shiort third man for a quick single.

LEG BYE! Variable bounce troubling the batters out there. Slower deliver, on a hard length and over middle and leg. This time the ball stays a bit low as Malan looks to hop and work iot leg side. Malan misses and the ball rolls onto the off side after hitting the thigh pads. The batters sneak in a leg bye.
Slower delivery, bowled into the pitch and over the stumps, this is tucked away through square leg for one more.

Drop and run! Good pace from Ngidi, at 139 clicks, on a shortish length and over middle and leg. The ball bounces a little extra once again. Dawid Malan does well to hop and just bunt it down towards silly point for a quick run.
Short of a length, angling in. The ball hurries onto Roy as he pulls it down to deep backward square leg for a single.
Extra bounce! This is bowled on a good length, around off. Jason Roy advances and looks to take it on but the ball just shoots up off the surface and leaves Roy bamboozled.
At the stumps, this is pushed towards silly mid on.
Dawid Malan is the new batter for England.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man! Keshav Maharaj bowls this one just a bit slower and angles it into leg stump. Jos Buttler looks to attempt the cut once again by going past the leg stump and gets another outside edge. This time it is a thick one and carries to the man at short third man. Lungi Ngidi takes a simple catch in front of him and bUttler departs once again for a low score.
Commentary.Howout: c Lungi Ngidi b Keshav Maharaj

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Edged away! This is angling into leg stump. Jos Buttler goes well past the leg stump, trying to cut it away. The ball takes the outside edge and goes past the keeper, into the third man fence.
Slower through the air and on a length, around middle. Roy nudges it to mid-wicket and sneaks in a quick run.
On middle and leg, Buttler comes forward and works it in front of square on the leg side for one.
Good fielding! This is flatter and angling into leg stump, Jason Roy gives himself a bit of room but can't beat the diving man at extra cover. Just a single t.n,.
Nicely bowled! Another slower ball, this time it's full and outside off. Jos Buttler looks to go hard it but is completely beaten.
Slower delivery, on a shorter length and over middle. Roy looks to pull but the ball goes off the higher part of the bat and towards mid-wicket. Single taken.
This is pitched up, outside off, Roy looks to go over mid off but mistimes it straight to the fielder over there.

Close but not close enough it seems. Ngidi goes bit wider and angles it into the pads. Jason Roy looks to flick it away but the ball nips back in a long way and pings him on the pads. There is a bit of an appeal from the bowler but it is turned down.
Excellent running! Around the top of off, Buttler pushes it towards mid off and races through for the single.
FOUR! Lungi Ngidi starts off with a loosener. This is on a length and angling down leg, Jos Buttler works it off his hips and picks up a boundary down to fine leg.
Change. Lungi Ngidi comes into the attack now.
Banged in short and over off at 145 clicks, Jason Roy pulls it in front of square on the leg side and picks up a comfortable two.
Good length, around off, this is punched out towards cover for a run.

This is poor from Keshav Maharaj and he has his hand up right away. Length, close to the off pole, Roy stays back and nudges it towards point for a quick run. Maharaj has a wild throw at the bowler's end and there's no one backing up there. The ball runs away into the fence and it will be five runs to Roy.
Pitches it a bit further up, around and almost touches 150 KPH, Buttler pushes it towards wide mid off and rotates the strike.
Length again, at 147 clicks and over middle, Roy tucks it away past square leg for just a single.
Anrich Nortje gets in his stride right away and serves a 146 KPH delivery, on a length and around the top of off. Roy has a tentative push at it as he plays it towards point.
Anrich Nortje to share the new ball.
Just a hint of flight, fuller and on middle. Jason Roy makes a bit of room and drives it down to long off for yet another single. A tidy first over from Keshav Maharaj, five singles off it.
Around off, Buttler strokes it through mid off and rotates the strike.
This is fired in on off stump, Roy drills it down to long off for one more.
Just drags back the length a bit and angles it into middle, Roy goes on the back foot to defend.
On off, Jos Buttler drives it on the up and through mid off for a single. Buttler is off the mark straightaway.
Maharaj starts off with a floater on leg stump, Jason Roy neatly clips it through mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single. England too are underway with that.
